newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon poll rerun still dogged by problems - voters.
newsitem.headline: Gabon poll rerun still dogged by problems - voters.

text.p: Polls opened in the Gabon capital Libreville on Sunday for a rerun of chaotic municipal elections but voting was again thrown into confusion by organisational problems, witnesses said.
Electoral lists and ballots were not available at most polling stations in the capital, which accounts for about half the electorate in the country of about 1.2 million people.
"Many names do not appear on the voter lists," a frustated voter said.
In one polling station, the voter list available was different from that of the National Elections Commission.
Polls opened officially at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) but three hours later some stations had still not received voter lists.
Turnout appeared even lower than the chaotic October 20 vote, with many politicians and some of their followers campaigning in the interior for December 1 legislative elections.
A rerun was also taking place in Fougamou, where a fight prevented voting on October 20. The election commission scrapped results in Libreville, blaming organisational problems.
No incident was reported on Sunday in Libreville or Fougamou.
President Omar Bongo's Gabonese Democratic Party and Father Paul M'Ba Abessole's opposition Woodcutters' Party won most seats decided last month.
The two parties are vying for control of Libreville city hall, with Abessole and Bongo's housing minister Jean-Francois Ntoutoume Emane battling for mayor.
